theme: The Transfiguration; the demonized boy; greatness in the Kingdom
readingInstruction: Read Mark 9:1-50. The Transfiguration, a father’s honest cry, a second prediction of the passion, and teaching on greatness and sin. Read verses 14 to 29 slowly, the story of the father and his son.
settingTheScene: Six days after Peter’s confession, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, and there they see his glory. They come down to find the other disciples in a dispute over a boy they could not heal. Throughout the chapter, the disciples do not understand. Jesus speaks again of his death, and they argue about who is the greatest.
observation: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him” (9:7).
“And Jesus said to him, If you can! All things are possible for one who believes” (9:23).
“This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer” (9:29).
“The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him. And when he is killed, after three days he will rise” (9:31).
“If anyone would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all” (9:35).
“Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for him if a great millstone were hung around his neck and he were cast into the sea” (9:42).
“Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another” (9:50).
interpretation:
On the mountain, Jesus is transfigured. His clothes become radiant, whiter than anyone could bleach them. Elijah and Moses appear and talk with him. Peter, terrified, suggests building three tents. A cloud overshadows them, and a voice from the cloud says, “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.” Suddenly they see only Jesus. The Law (Moses) and the Prophets (Elijah) bear witness to Jesus, and then they fade. The Father’s command is to listen to the Son. On the way down, Jesus tells them not to tell anyone until the Son of Man has risen from the dead. They do not understand what rising from the dead means.

At the foot of the mountain, a father has brought his son, who has a spirit that seizes him, throws him down, and makes him mute. The disciples could not cast it out. The father says to Jesus, “If you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.” Jesus says, “If you can! All things are possible for one who believes.” And the father cries out one of the most honest prayers in the Bible: “I believe; help my unbelief!” He has faith, but it is mixed with doubt, and he brings both to Jesus. Jesus does not reject him. He rebukes the spirit, and the boy is freed. When the disciples ask why they could not, Jesus says, “This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer.”

Jesus again speaks of his death and resurrection, and they do not understand and are afraid to ask. Instead, on the road they have argued about who is greatest. Jesus sits down, calls the Twelve, and says, “If anyone would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.” He takes a child in his arms and says that whoever receives such a child in his name receives him.

The chapter ends with stern warnings. John reports someone casting out demons in Jesus’ name who was not following them, and Jesus says, “Whoever is not against us is for us.” Then he warns against causing little ones to stumble, and calls his followers to take radical action against sin: if your hand or foot or eye causes you to sin, cut it off or pluck it out. The point is not self-mutilation but the seriousness of sin. “Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
connection: Exodus 24:15-18 and 34:29-35 describe Moses on the mountain in glory. Malachi 4:5 promises Elijah. Deuteronomy 18:15 says to listen to the prophet like Moses. 2 Peter 1:16-18 is Peter’s reflection on the Transfiguration. Luke 9:31 says Moses and Elijah spoke of his departure. Psalm 73:23-26 is a prayer of the weak but trusting. Jude 22 calls us to have mercy on those who doubt. Philippians 2:3-8 shows the servant attitude.
application:
Pray the father’s prayer from your heart: “I believe; help my unbelief!” Be honest about both.

Listen to Jesus today. Read one of his teachings in the Gospels slowly.

Ask where you have been arguing about greatness, and take the servant’s place.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you listen to his beloved Son.
Ask him to teach you to pray.
